title: Constitutional Litigation (Writ)
copy: Constitutional and public law representation before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.
valueProp: Careful assessment of unlawful public action, identification of appropriate constitutional remedies and strategic representation throughout judicial review proceedings.
overview: Our Writ practice focuses on constitutional and public law remedies before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.

We advise and represent individuals, businesses and organisations seeking judicial review of unlawful actions, decisions and omissions of public authorities, as well as protection of constitutional and legal rights.
We represent clients in constitutional and administrative law matters involving government authorities, statutory bodies, public officials and other entities exercising public functions.

services.title: Writ Appeals & Related Proceedings
services.copy: Representation in appeals and other proceedings arising from judgments, orders and decisions of the High Court Division in constitutional and administrative matters.

faqs.q: When can a writ petition be filed?
faqs.a: A writ petition may be appropriate where a public authority or other entity exercising public functions has acted unlawfully, exceeded its jurisdiction, failed to perform a legal duty or infringed a legal or constitutional right. The availability of the remedy depends on the facts and applicable law.

faqs.q: Can a government decision be challenged through a writ?
faqs.a: Yes, in appropriate circumstances. Government and administrative decisions may be subject to judicial review where they are unlawful, made without jurisdiction, procedurally improper or otherwise amenable to constitutional review.

faqs.q: Can I file a writ against a private person or company?
faqs.a: Writ jurisdiction primarily concerns public authorities and the exercise of public functions. Whether a particular private entity or action falls within the scope of constitutional judicial review depends on the nature of the function and the applicable legal framework.

faqs.q: Can a writ petition stop an unlawful government action?
faqs.a: In appropriate cases, the High Court Division may grant interim or other appropriate relief to protect the petitioner's position while the matter is being considered. The availability and scope of such relief depend on the circumstances of each case.

faqs.q: Do I need to challenge the decision through another legal remedy first?
faqs.a: Not necessarily in every case. The maintainability of a writ petition may depend on the availability and adequacy of alternative remedies, the nature of the impugned action and other legal considerations. We assess these issues before recommending the appropriate course of action.
